item.title: Beyond Time Induction: Structured Conditional Neural Solvers for Parametric Stochastic-Volatility Pricing
item.description: arXiv:2610.19254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Physics-informed neural networks provide a flexible framework for learning parametric PDE solution families without labeled data, yet preserving accurate derivatives across heterogeneous regimes remains challenging. Structured neural solvers offer compact representations, but restrictive conditional parameterizations can limit adaptation across the solution family. We introduce BeTINN, a structured conditional architecture extending time-induced modulation through multi-directional time-parameter conditioning and a joint residual pathway. We evaluate BeTINN on the Heston stochastic-volatility PDE, a demanding parametric problem with mixed derivatives and economically relevant first- and second-order sensitivities. BeTINN improves joint accuracy across normalized option value and key sensitivity metrics relative to our baselines. Controlled ablations characterize the roles of its architectural components. We further find that validation physics loss is informative but does not fully determine differential fidelity, and that accurate solution values can coexist with localized derivative errors. These results support structured conditional adaptation and motivate derivative-aware evaluation when sensitivities are downstream quantities of interest.
item.dc:creator: Jose Miguel Lara Rangel, Mixtli Vazquez Mendoza

item.title: Insights on Time-consistent Deep Hedging under Elicitable Dynamic Risk Measures
item.description: arXiv:2609.02014v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study deep hedging where the objective is expressed in terms of a dynamic risk measure, under which sequential decisions are time-consistent. We tackle the problem of basket option hedging. We show that the approach is feasible and can be used conveniently in the presence of more complex state spaces with higher dimension than what was previously test in the literature. We rely on the conditional elicitability of spectral risk measures to represent the optimization objective. We provide insights on how the choice of scoring function impacts the training of the hedging agent. We also propose an adapted reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm to solve the problem, which contains additions that are crucial to a successful training of the deep RL agent, and without which the agent fails to converge to proper solutions. The time-consistent hedging strategies are also benchmarked against deep hedging approaches relying on static risk measures leading to precommitment.
item.dc:creator: Shuyi Zhang, Fr\'ed\'eric Godin

item.title: The Efficient Frontier from a LASSO Solver
item.description: arXiv:2609.37108v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Schmelzer and Hastie prove that Markowitz's Critical Line Algorithm and the LASSO path trace the same curve. This companion note checks that result numerically with a stock LASSO solver, \texttt{lars\_path} from \texttt{scikit-learn}, and no portfolio software. It covers long--short portfolios under a leverage cap, fixed leverage with varying risk appetite, and the classical long-only, fully invested frontier. Every corner the path returns meets its own optimality conditions to about $10^{-13}$ and agrees with independent quadratic-programming solvers, on factor models of up to 500 assets, on the Fama--French size and book-to-market portfolios, and on daily returns of 494 S\&P~500 stocks. Called naively, the long-only path stops at the maximum-Sharpe portfolio. One shift of the response, by an amount computed in advance, lets a single call reach the minimum-variance portfolio. The script, its checks, the Fama--French returns and an R cross-check are published, with a locked environment, so that anyone can repeat them.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Schmelzer

item.title: Deep kernel hedging
item.description: arXiv:2609.34474v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We introduce a deep kernel hedging framework that combines the flexibility of deep learning with the structural inductive bias of kernel methods. The hedging functional is restricted to a reproducing kernel Hilbert space whose kernel is parameterized through a neural network embedding of the input features. The framework minimizes a regularized empirical risk under convex loss functions and can accommodate path-dependent information through truncated time-augmented signature features. We derive a generalized representer theorem for the joint hedging problem, reducing the empirical optimization to a finite-dimensional problem. To further reduce the computational cost associated with large kernel matrices, we develop a scalable random Fourier feature approximation and establish convergence guarantees. The random Fourier parameters are sampled once and remain fixed throughout training, while the deep kernel adapts to market data through the learned neural representation. We evaluate the performance of the proposed deep kernel approach on both synthetic and real data and compare it with standard kernel methods and classical deep hedging architectures. Numerical results indicate competitive and robust hedging performance, particularly in low-data regimes, which highlights the benefits of combining expressive neural representations with the inductive bias of kernel methods.
item.dc:creator: Jean-Loup Dupret, Donatien Hainaut, Edouard Motte
